In October 2024, I took our 13-year-old dog to Myllyveti for an ultrasound at the request of our own veterinarian. The dog had a heart defect and fluid in his stomach. During the ultrasound, the dog was held on its back for a long time, causing it to breathe poorly. The veterinarian announced that the dog's condition was so bad that it could no longer be taken home, but that it would have to be euthanized.

I went out, shocked by the news, to call my wife when the veterinarian said that he would give our dog supplemental oxygen. When we got back to Myllyveti, the dog was completely out of sorts, drugged and pawing at the walls - it had clearly been given a sedative without asking me. My wife no longer saw our dog as normal before the dog's death.

While we were saying goodbye to the dog as he lay on the floor of the examination room on a mattress, the veterinarian came in to talk about the bill and ask what kind of urn we wanted. So the dog was still alive in its last moments and the idlers will be questioned!

You wouldn't think such clumsy behavior would exist in a company that charges hundreds of euros for every little movement they make. The company is owned by foreign investors. I would never take my own pet to a large chain company for treatment again. It's worth choosing private, small veterinary clinics.

It's also worth googling the company name.
I felt pretty screwed. They kept trying to sell me some additional services and the price for just the lab test was 320€. I will never go to the same shop again and I will not recommend it to anyone.
